member.name: T:TrueAutomation.Core.WCF.NHibernate.SessionManagementServiceBehavior
member.summary: Provides a mechanism to modify or insert custom extensions across an entire service, including the ServiceHostBase. We implement this class to bootstrap the initialization of a service class by inserting NHibernate session management facilities into the service.
Provides the ability to pass custom data to binding elements to support the contract implementation.
member.param: The service description of the service.
The host of the service.
The service endpoints.
Custom objects to which binding elements have access.
member.remarks:
Use the AddBindingParameters method to add custom data objects to the parameters collection that binding elements can use to acquire extra information to enable them to support the contract.
This method is called once for each listen URI. For example, if a service has four endpoints, and two of them have the same listen URI, then this method gets called three times. The reason is that the bindingParameters target each channel stack and there is one channel stack for each listen URI. Because each call receives those endpoints at that listen URI, two calls each get a single , and one call gets a collection of two
objects.

member.name: T:TrueAutomation.Core.WCF.NHibernate.DispatchMessageInspector
member.summary: Defines the methods that enable custom inspection or modification of inbound and outbound application messages in service applications. This implementation ensures that all NHibernate sessions for the current instance context are closed before the response is sent back to the client. This guards against resource leaks and other unexpected behavior caused by errors, exceptions, sloppiness, etc.

member.summary: Called after an inbound message has been received but before the message is dispatched to the intended operation.
member.param: The request message.
The incoming channel.

member.returns: The object used to correlate state. This object is passed back in the BeforeSendReply method.
member.remarks: Use the AfterReceiveRequest method to inspect or modify the incoming message, the client channel that provided it, and the current service instance. The return value can be any object that you want to use for correlation purposes; it is returned to you as the correlationState parameter in the BeforeSendReply method.

member.summary: Enables an extension object to find out when it has been aggregated. Called when the extension is added to the property.

member.remarks: Use this method to keep track of the object to which the current instance of the extension belongs. This call gives extensions a chance to handle events or inspect properties of their owner.

member.name: M:TrueAutomation.Core.WCF.NHibernate.SessionExtension.System#ServiceModel#IExtension{System#ServiceModel#InstanceContext}#Detach(System.ServiceModel.InstanceContext)
member.summary: Enables an extension object to find out when it is no longer aggregated. Called when the extension is added to the property.
member.param: The extensible object that aggregates this extension.
member.remarks:
Use the Detach method to find out when the extension has been removed. An extension can use this to unhook events on the extensible object. An extension can also throw from this method to indicate that, once added, the extension cannot be removed.
Note that this method is not called when the owner object is disposed or closed. If needed, it is up to the extension or the code adding the extension to hook the appropriate events or implement the appropriate interfaces (for ) to observe the lifecycle of the owner.
